Enterprise agentic AI is seeing massive growth.

The enterprise agentic AI market is now expected to grow from $2.6 billion to $24.5 billion by 2030, increasing more than 9x.

These systems can effectively reason and execute with minimal human oversight.

By 2028, 30% of enterprise applications are expected to embed autonomous agents, per Gartner forecasts.

Adoption is expected to expand across customer service, operations, finance, HR, and cybersecurity.

The biggest shift is that AI is moving from simply assisting humans to actually executing and orchestrating work.

This could materially reduce operating costs and improve operational efficiency.

Agentic AI is a major catalyst for corporate efficiency.

When fading a breakout, it is usually very difficult to time the top of a move. So the strategy utilizes averaging down as the move develops.

Averaging down is the way to the poor house.

If fading breakouts (going against the momentum) is your strategy, make sure you have an uncle point. 

Without an uncle point, I have seen so many similar strategies needing funding/fresh capital to stay in business.

There are two reasons I still use X
1. It is important for traders to constantly preach "best practices" to themselves -- I mean daily, hourly, trade by trade
2. Putting thoughts into typed words helps me work through the details of a trade
There is a third -- and that is rare courteous and thoughtful engagement. These are far rarer than 10 or 15 years ago
Today, everyone's a genius

I can only speak for myself on trading. Every great trader I know - and via Chicago pits, Commodities Corp and Market Wizards I think I know a lot of them - developed their own niche. They didn't simply discover a niche. They invented their own and kept working on the niche

Wow. Super assumptive. You do know I am all but crippled, don't you

Close to 80 years old. Physically disabled - wheelchair at airport, walker when shopping, walking stick at home. Losing parts of my memory bank, little bit hard of hearing. Mostly at doctors appointments when not at the computer. 
Been supporting myself from the futures markets since 1975 when Gerald Ford took the office of president of the US when Tricky Dick Nixon resigned and Microsoft was founded.

Thinking about retiring in a couple ways

Not from futures trading company's for my own personal account. Probably will never quit. It's good I always carry stop orders on every position I hold.

Personal on Twitter X is a yes for quitting - the way I think about trading is mostly thought of as arcane by the "moderns" - surprised because it works better than it might have in the early 1900s. Thoughtful engagement on X is all but history

Probably phase out, then quit on Teaching -- there just are not that many people interested in learning the geometrically-described hieroglyphics of price discovery of the olden days. I have seen during my time dozens of schemes for trading come, then go
